# aeneid-086 — drafter's notes (XI.445–531)

33 units, 87 lines; `t` cut by `A.cut` in `make_units.py`; all script checks pass with no warnings (EXEMPT and
NOSTOP units deliberately skipped, below). Part name "Turnus to Arms; Camilla's Offer (XI.445–531)"; Latin title
"Turnus ad arma. Camilla". One Greenough paragraph (445), `p: true` on the first unit.

## Speech marks
- Turnus to the council: 459–461, one unit (459–462, which also carries the narrative 'Nec plura locutus… altis'
  so that the misprinted closing mark stays inside one unit). Rule 5b: the print encloses the whole of 459,
  `ait` and `Turnus` included (`“Immo, ait, O cives adrepto tempore, Turnus,”`), reopens before `cogite` (460),
  and joins the closing mark to `Nec` (461 `”Nec`). t kept as printed; l/i open at 'Oh yes', set "says/said
  Turnus, seizing the moment" outside the marks, reopen at 'citizens'/'call', close after 'ruunt.'. The mark
  counts happen to match (2/2) but the unit is exempt because the marks are moved. Note opens with the print's
  reading (described in words; the n check forbids double marks in notes, so `”Nec` is not quoted literally).
- Turnus's orders: 463–467, units 463 and 464. Rule 5b: second opening mark before `duc` (464) inside a running
  speech; l/i set "he says" outside marks. Unit 463 note opens with the print's reading. Closes at 467 `arma.”`
  as printed (unit 464, marks match).
- Matrons' prayer: 483–485, one unit, marks as printed. 486 `Cingitur…` is narrative (own unit).
- Camilla: 502–506 (units 502, 505), as printed. Turnus's reply: 508–519 (units 508, 509, 511, 515, 517), as printed.
- EXEMPT = {459, 463}.

## Unit that ends without a stop
- 492–493 ends at `aperto` with no punctuation. Greenough prints the horse simile 492–497 as one six-line period
  whose only internal mark is the comma after `luxurians` (497), so a ≤5-line unit is impossible without a cut at
  an unpunctuated point. Split where the 'aut… aut' alternatives begin; the note says so. Exempted from the
  ending check as NOSTOP = {492}. A reviewer may prefer a 6-line unit instead; I could not find a better cut.

## Latin Library variants
- 469 `Consilium`/`concilium`: sense differs (plan abandoned vs council left); noted, print kept.
- 463 `maniplos`/`maniplis`: construction differs (acc.+inf. vs dative), sense barely; noted briefly.
- 466 `firmet… capessat`/`firment… capessant`: no sense change; one clause in the note, as asked.
- Others (`adrectae`, `adrepto`, `adceperit`, `adsciverit`, `adcinxerat`, `praesaepia`, `adrectisque`, `siqua`,
  `adcommoda`): orthography; flagged as Greenough's spellings, not as variants.

## Doubtful readings / interpretations kept
- No misprint in the words themselves found. 467 `qua iusso` = iussero (old future perfect), explained.
- 495 `aquae` taken as probably dative with `adsuetus` (genitive possible).
- 529 `instare iugis`: both 'press on from the ridges' and 'stand on the ridges' given in the note.
- 486 `certatim` of a single man: explained as 'with all eagerness'; no authority cited.
- 516 `bivias… fauces`: taken as a pass with an entrance at each end.
